content.text: The cause is in the `br` inline rule. Its match is only `"  \n"` (or `"\\\n"`), so the next line's leading whitespace is left in the stream and rendered as text. I'll extend the rule to also consume leading spaces and tabs on the continuation line.

content.text:
I fixed the bug in `src/rules.ts`. I couldn't run the tests because the folder has no `node_modules`, so the change is verified by reading the code only. **Cause:** the inline `br` rule, `const br = /^( {2,}|\\)\n(?!\s*$)/;` at `src/rules.ts:286`, matched only the trailing spaces or backslash and the newline. The leading whitespace of the next line was left in the stream and was tokenized as text, which produced `
bar`. **Fix:** the rule now also consumes any spaces and tabs at the start of the continuation line: ```ts const br = /^( {2,}|\\)\n(?!\s*$)[ \t]*/; ``` The existing `(?!\s*$)` lookahead is unchanged, so a break before a whitespace-only line still isn't treated as a hard break. The GFM `breaks` variant rewrites `{2,}` to `*` and still gets the same trailing `[ \t]*`, so it is covered too. `Tokenizer.br` returns `raw: cap[0]`, so the consumed whitespace is part of the token. The parser only renders `
` from that token, so the output for `foo \n bar` becomes `

foo
bar

`. The backslash and tab cases go through the same regex and are fixed the same way. I didn't add tests, as you asked. Running the existing suite (`npm test`) once dependencies are installed would confirm nothing else changed.
